messages:
Amanda Chen: quick follow-up to the packaging RFC 3 thinking about a 'slabbed image' pattern for on-prem bundles so rollforwards and patch streams are tiny in strict airgapped sites. idea: immutable base slab + small incremental content-addressed slabs. activation becomes an atomic slab swap.

Raul Gomez: sounds promising. how would the operator/agent handshake work over flaky media (USB / intermittent rsync)? need resume semantics.

Amanda Chen: flow sketch: operator publishes a signed slab index; agent verifies signature and capability table; agent requests missing chunks in parallel; each chunk fetch supports range/resume and returns a resume token on failure. operator can resume by referencing the token.

Jia Patel: verification: full sha256 per chunk vs merkle proofs? merkle helps avoid re-downloading large files but adds index complexity and CPU for low-end appliances.

Kevin O'Neill: agree. make verifier configurable. default sha256 per chunk (simpler), optional merkle for minimal-transfer sites. config example below:

```yaml
packaging:
  slab_index_signing: pgp
  chunk_verifier: sha256  # or merkle
  slab_retention: 2
  activation_window: 30m
```

Nikhil: rollback approach: keep a tiny local activation journal that records applied file-level deltas and manifest sequence. if activation fails mid-apply we reverse-replay the journal. journal is bounded (configurable cap) and much smaller than full slabs.

Raul Gomez: nice3 ensures rollbacks are local and don't require re-downloading previous slabs in airgapped setups. need canonical apply ordering and idempotent operations.

Jia Patel: also cap the journal; and keep a pinned last-known-good slab separate on disk so we can immediate revert without fetch.

Amanda Chen: operator UX: builders output slab index + chunk store. operator tooling will have `push-slab` and `apply-slab`. for customers that prefer a single cassette (ship on media) we support a cassette wrapper (tarball of slabstore + signed index) which unpacks into slabs on the receiving side and verifies.

Kevin O'Neill: chunk reuse vs diffs: prefer content-addressed chunk reuse. diffs like bsdiff can be smaller but are risky across arch/fs variations and costly to compute. CA chunks give dedupe across versions.

Raul Gomez: security: index must be signed and include signer fingerprint + timestamp. chunk signatures optional but recommended for paranoid deployments. audit metadata should be attached to index.

sre-bot: deploy-bot: slab-upload CI passed for build-1345: 42 chunks produced, index sig OK :white_check_mark: (https://ci.redwood.dev/build/1345)

Jia Patel: transport API: POST /v1/slab/index (signed), then GET /v1/slab/chunk/:hash with Accept-Ranges: bytes for resume. agent should advertise supported verifier (sha256/merkle) and max concurrent fetches. keep HTTP-friendly so proxies and offline proxies can be used.

Kevin O'Neill: metrics to collect: slab.chunk.size_histogram, slab.resume.count, slab.activation.duration, slab.rollback.count. use these to pick chunk size defaults. smaller chunk = better resume but higher metadata overhead.

Amanda Chen: one more operational idea: pre-activation sandbox dry-run that applies changes to a tmp mount and runs quick sanity checks before flipping active symlink. catches obvious failures without requiring rollback.

Raul Gomez: can we fit this into the current packaging RFC without breaking existing single-tar installs? propose an appendix describing on-disk layout, journal format, operator CLI, and API contract.

Amanda Chen: yes. Kevin will draft appendix. @Jia @Raul please review when posted. aiming to land in packaging RFC repo by EOD Wed.

Jia Patel: will review.

Raul Gomez: will review too. thanks! :sparkles:
